extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners (users of the Enforcement Rules of the Korean Patent Act)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed enforcement-rule guidance on formalities examination, return/invalidation of application documents, amendment and restoration procedures, and discontinuation/resumption of patent-related proceedings under the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 11 — Return of Illegitimate Application Document (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application or related document falls under any of the subparagraphs listed in Article 11, the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial and Appeal Board shall not deem such application documents to be legitimate (except for special provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general authority under which specific illegitimacy criteria (items 1–20) are applied and documents may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 1 — Violation of Enforcement Rules Article 2 / improper document preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Article 2 of the Enforcement Rules is violated and a document is not prepared per an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents not prepared in accordance with required formats or content under Article 2 may be deemed illegitimate and returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 2 — Unclear application/document type
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the type of an application or a document is not clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the document's nature/type cannot be ascertained, it may be treated as illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 3 — Missing name/applicant code/address
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the name (or title for a juristic person) or the applicant code of a person who conducts a patent-related proceeding (or in absence of code, name and address/title and business address) is not indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient identification of the applicant renders the document illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 4 — Non-Korean language application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is not written in Korean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be in Korean unless otherwise allowed; non-Korean filings can be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 5 — Missing specification or description
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification is not attached to an application (including where the description of the invention is not included in the specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application lacking the specification/description is illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 5-2 — Specification without claims after amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification which does not include the claims is attached to a patent application filed by the lawful holder of a right and the amendment period of the specification under Article 42(2)(ii) has already elapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are missing and the amendment period has passed, the filing is illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 6 — Foreign submitter without domicile/place of business in Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application document was submitted by a person who has neither a domicile nor a place of business in the Republic of Korea, other than a patent administrator under Article 5(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by foreign persons without required Korean domicile/business (and not authorized administrators) may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 7 — Late submission beyond designated period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the documents were not submitted within the designated period under the Patent Act or any order under the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely submissions can be treated as illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 8 — Request for extension of non-extendable period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extension of the period was submitted for the period not allowed for extension among the periods stipulated under the Patent Act or any order under the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to extend non-extendable periods are invalid and may cause return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 9 — Late extension request for trial periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extension of the period was submitted after the expiration of the period for requesting a trial under Article 132(17) or the period designated by the Commissioner/President/administrative judge or examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late extension requests for trial-request periods are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 10 — Submission after termination of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents regarding a patent-related proceeding have been submitted after the termination of such patent-related proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents filed after proceeding termination may be returned as illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 11 — Unauthorized person submitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person not entitled to carry out a patent-related proceeding has submitted documents regarding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only entitled persons may submit documents; unauthorized submissions are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 12 — Unclear / unacceptable specific annexed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where concerned documents such as the report in Annexed Form No.2 (restriction of reliance on general power of attorney), application for registration of general power of attorney (Annexed Form No.3), application for change/withdrawal of registration of general power of attorney, application for grant of applicant code (Annexed Form No.4) or ex officio are not clear and cannot be accepted when an application code should be granted based on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unclear or unacceptable annexed-form submissions can be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 13 — Electronic submission not using KIPO software or unreadable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application or document submitted over a computerized network or via electronic recording device is not prepared by using the software offered by KIPO or the KIPO website, or where electronic documents have been submitted in a condition where they cannot be handled in the electronic data processing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filings must comply with KIPO software/format requirements or they may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 13-2 — Failure to submit required documents under Article 3(2)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents required to be submitted under Article 3(2)(ii) of the Enforcement Rules have not been submitted within the designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing required documents under specific rule provisions causes illegitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 14 — Failure to submit documents under Article 8 within allowed explanation period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents required to be submitted under Article 8 of the Enforcement Rules have not been submitted within the period allowed for explanation without any legitimate explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required documents in the explanation window (without legitimate reason) can render the filing illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 15 — Request for examination attached to specification without claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent applicant has submitted a request for examination on a patent application attached with a specification which does not include the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for examination with a specification lacking claims is illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 16 — Early publication request for patent without claims or for already-registered patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for early publication has been submitted for a patent application attached with a description which does not include claims or a patent registered for publication under Article 87(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early publication requests require claims (and cannot be made for already-registered patents in that context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 17 — Circumstances requiring immediate grant decision (Article 40(2)(i) sub-subparagraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a decision to grant a patent cannot be delayed since the application falls under any of the sub-subparagraphs of Article 40(2)(i) of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain cases require immediate grant decision and therefore documents falling under this may be handled specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 18 — Circumstances prohibiting deferral of examination (Article 40(3)(iii) sub-subparagraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examination on a patent application cannot be deferred since the application falls under any of the sub-subparagraphs of Article 40(3)(iii) of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application falls under these urgent categories, usual deferral rules do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 19 — Request for re-examination without amendment or prohibited by Article 67(2)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for re-examination without amendment of a specification or drawing(s) attached to a patent application has been made or where a request for re-examination cannot be made since the application falls under Article 67(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper re-examination requests or those barred by rule will be treated as illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimacy criterion 20 — Missing Korean translation or subject to Article 52/53/59/64 provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: According to proviso 1, Article 52 of the Patent Act, where the Korean translation is not yet submitted or where it is subject to Article 53(1)(ii), Article 59(2)(ii) or Article 64(2)(ii) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing Korean translation where required can make an application illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement before returning illegitimate documents (Article 11(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application documents are to be returned as illegitimate under Article 11(1), the Commissioner or President shall deliver a notice containing the intention to return, grounds for return and period for explanation to the applicants. If certain subparagraphs apply (Article 11(1)(xiv)), immediate notification and return must occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive a notice with reasons and an opportunity to explain except in specified immediate-return cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant explanation or request for return procedures (Article 11(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who receives returned documents and wishes to explain must submit an explanation in Annexed Form No.24 within the period for explanation. If the applicant wishes to receive returned documents without explanation, submit Annexed Form No.8; the commissioner/president shall immediately return the documents on such request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified annexed forms and observe the explanation period; immediate return is available upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning after failure to explain (Article 11(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant fails to submit an explanation or request for return within the period for explanation, or where submitted explanations are groundless, the Commissioner/president shall return the application documents immediately after expiration of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of timely or legitimate explanation leads to prompt return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination — definition and remit
rubrics_metrics.description: A formalities examination is a review procedure conducted regarding a patent-related proceeding under Article 46 of the Patent Act and Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules. If irregularities are found, the commissioner/president shall order amendment and may invalidate the proceeding or return application documents after giving opportunity to explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities exam focuses on procedural compliance; substantive issues may be handled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination — who conducts and transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle formalities examinations are conducted by the divisions in charge (Application Division, International Application Division, Registration Division, Trial Policy Division) under the Commissioner or President. Where irregularities are closely linked to substantive examinations, an examiner conducts the formalities examination. If examiner omits/forwards items, the division completes the formalities exam and re-transfers to examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is coordination and transfer between divisions and examiners depending on linkage to substantive matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceeding — examiner requests amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent-related proceeding falls under any subparagraph of Article 46, an examiner shall request amendment of such proceeding in the name of the Commissioner. The request shall state intention to invalidate, items to be amended, contents in violation of procedural requirements, and, if necessary, amendment methods. The amendment period shall be within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for amendment must be detailed; standard amendment period is one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of submitting amendment within designated period
rubrics_metrics.description: If irregularities are addressed through submission of an amendment within the designated period, the application shall be deemed amended when the proceeding was conducted. If not submitted or irregularities remain, an examiner can invalidate the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and adequate amendment cures the irregularity; otherwise invalidation may follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of amendment submitted after designated period but before invalidation notice (①)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the expiration of the designated period, if irregularities are addressed by submitting an amendment before the delivery date of a notice of invalidation ('date of invalidation'), the examiner shall not invalidate the application but accept it. An amendment submitted after the date of invalidation shall be returned. If mailed before date of invalidation but overlooked, examiner shall revoke the invalidation and accept the amendment. Amendments submitted on the date of invalidation are treated the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late mailed amendments received before invalidation may be accepted; date-of-invalidation is the cutoff; examiner must correct oversights.

rubrics_metrics.name: New procedural irregularities found after amendment (②)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new irregularities are found when amendment is completed, the examiner shall set a period for such irregularities and request amendment again. Applicant shall pay amendment fees for each amendment. Exception: if items omitted in the first amendment are ordered amended again, additional fees for those items are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple amendment rounds may incur fees except for omitted first-time items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendments irrelevant to request (③)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a voluntary amendment irrelevant to the intention of the amendment request is submitted while a written amendment for the request has not been submitted, the examiner shall accept the voluntary amendment. If amended items fall under items for which amendment fees are paid, the amendment fee shall be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary, non-requested amendments can be accepted but may trigger fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial amendments addressing only some requested items (④)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examiner requests amendment to more than two proceedings in a single request and the applicant amends only parts within the period, the examiner shall invalidate only the proceedings of which irregularities are not addressed. Separate amendments in multiple submissions are treated as separate amendments and fees apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete amendments result in selective invalidation; multiple amendments can increase fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of amended items without proper amendment formalities (⑤)
rubrics_metrics.description: If only amended items are submitted without using the formalities of an amendment, an examiner shall accept the document first, then request amendment to the amendment proceeding citing formalities violation. If the type of document is unclear, return it. Where irregularities are minor, examiner can accept without requesting amendment. If formalities violation is not corrected within designated period, examiner shall invalidate the amendment proceeding; if irregularities indicated by invalidation are not addressed, invalidate the concerned proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical/formal defects are handled flexibly but uncorrected formal violations may lead to invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to invalidate — who may invalidate
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who can invalidate a patent-related proceeding is the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial and Appeal Board, not an examiner. Subjects of invalidation are all patent-related proceedings, not limited to application proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners recommend invalidation but final invalidation decision rests with Commissioner/President; examiner must state grounds and notify the person who conducted the proceeding and attach notice of right to administrative trial/lawsuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation when additional examination fees unpaid after claim increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Where additional payment of examination fees is required to an applicant since the number of claims is increased because of amendments to the description after a request for examination made by a person other than the applicant, but the applicant has not paid the examination fees, an examiner shall invalidate the amendment proceeding for a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay extra fees triggered by claim increases can cause invalidation of amendment proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of invalidation (legal consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is invalidated, the application is deemed never to have been filed for purposes of Articles 36(1)–(3). An application claiming Domestic Priority cannot be filed based on inventions disclosed in description/drawings originally attached. When invalidated, the right to request compensation is deemed never to have existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation has retroactive, consequential effects on filing status, priority, and compensation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of invalidation — grounds and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a proceeding is invalidated but failure to amend within designated period is recognized to have been caused by reasons not attributable to the person ordered to amend, the Commissioner can revoke invalidation if a request is made within two months of the day such unavoidable causes cease. However, if one year has elapsed after the designated period expired, revocation cannot be made. 'Causes not attributable' refer to reasons ordinary persons cannot avoid (natural disasters, unavoidable reasons) and cases where invalidation document was delivered to an uninvolved party. Applicant's unawareness of service is generally not included unless particular reason exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict time limits; only unavoidable non-attributable causes (e.g., natural disasters) support revocation; laches/unawareness generally not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches waiver note (relation to Article 16(2) / former Article 32(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The so-called 'laches waiver' applies only where the Commissioner invalidates a proceeding, except where person intentionally passed designated period or failed to pay patent fees at registration time. Laches waiver does not apply where a patent right is extinguished due to failure to pay patent fees in additional payment period (citing case law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits exist for invoking laches-based relief; consult specific statutory/case law contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting revocation (Form No.10 and evidentiary documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant wishes revocation of invalidation, attach copy of evidential document for reasons of laches to a written request in Annexed Form No.10 and submit to Commissioner. If legal representative present, attach copy of power of representation evidential document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified form and provide supporting evidence (and proof of representation when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and effects on amendment period after revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to revoke invalidation is determined by the examiner/division that invalidated the application in the first place under the name of the Commissioner/President. The examiner/division shall notify the requester. The notification shall state that amendment can be made within the period corresponding to the original amendment period from time of revocation of invalidation. Where proceedings or examinations were conducted after invalidation but before revocation, examiner shall review whether such proceedings/examinations take effect considering revocation and confidence protection principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation restores opportunity to amend within time corresponding to original period; examiner must assess effects of interim acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of documents — notification contents and immediate return on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner/President shall deliver notification stating intention to return application documents, ground for rejection and period for explanation to the applicant. If applicant wishes to receive returned documents without giving an explanation within the period, submit request for return (Form No.8) and the Commissioner/President shall return documents immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may choose immediate return instead of explanation using specified form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of documents after failure to explain or groundless explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to submit explanation or request for return within period for explanation, or explanation is deemed groundless, Commissioner/President shall return application documents right after expiration of the period for explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, legitimate explanation is necessary to avoid return; otherwise immediate return follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may submit explanation/opinion but not amendment in response to return notice
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can submit an explanation or opinion on the notice of grounds for rejection within the period for explanation. However, he/she is not allowed to submit an amendment in order to address the grounds for rejection of application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses to return-notices are limited to explanations/opinions (no substantive amendments at that stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on substantive matters vs formalities on return decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters to be amended in proceedings include irregularities in items of applications and failure to prepare required documents. Other than these formalities, substantive issues (e.g., whether foreigners hold capacity or whether applicant can obtain a patent in a joint invention) shall not be included; therefore substantive matters shall not be immediately rejected. Application documents containing substantive matters shall be accepted first, and then an examiner shall conduct a substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities examiners must not prematurely reject on substantive grounds; accept and then substantively examine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent completion of proceeding (when missed due to non-attributable cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where person who conducted a proceeding failed to comply with the period for requesting a trial (Article 132(17)) or demanding a retrial (Article 180(1)) because of a cause not attributable to the person, he/she may subsequently complete the proceeding within the designated period. The period allowed is within 2 months of the day when cause not attributable ceases. When one year has elapsed from the day of expiration of the period for subsequently completing, the proceeding cannot be completed subsequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent completion is allowed for non-attributable reasons, subject to 2-month window after cause ends and an overall one-year bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patent application (Article 67(3)) — filing for examination/reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant fails to comply with a period due to reasons not attributable and this leads to revocation of application or confirmation of rejection, applicant may file a request on examination or reexamination within two months from date on which such grounds cease. However, if one year has passed from the expiration date of the concerned period, the applicant shall not file. Relevant periods include: (1) period allowed for request of examination pursuant to Article 59(2) or (3), and (2) period allowed for request of reexamination pursuant to Article 67(2)(i). Notwithstanding Article 59(5), where such request is filed under paragraph 1, the application shall be deemed not to have been withdrawn or the decision to reject deemed not to have become final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration windows: two months after cause ends, with a one-year absolute limit; filing restores application status for purposes of withdrawal/rejection in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 5 — Discontinuation and resumption: definitions (interruption vs suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discontinuation of a patent-related proceeding means it does not legally proceed before completion. The Patent Act divides discontinuation into interruption and suspension. Interruption: when a cause attributable to a party prevents conducting the proceeding until another party conducts it. Suspension: when a cause affecting KIPO or a party makes the proceeding suspended legally or by KIPO decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish interruption (party-caused pauses) and suspension (office-caused or indefinite obstacles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption of proceeding — statutory causes (Article 20 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding is interrupted in any of: 1) relevant party dies; 2) relevant corporate party dissolves in merger; 3) relevant party loses capacity to perform proceeding; 4) party's legal representative dies or loses power; 5) duty of the party as trustee terminates; 6) representative appointed under proviso to Article 11(1) excluding subparagraphs dies or becomes disqualified; 7) bankruptcy trustee or intervening qualified person becomes disqualified or dies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the enumerated legal causes that trigger interruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of interrupted proceeding — who may resume (Article 21 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceeding interrupted under Article 20, persons who shall resume include: 1) in death cases — deceased party's heir, administrator of inherited property, or person authorized under any Act (except heir may not resume while renunciation period active); 2) in merger dissolution — surviving/new corporation; 3) in reinstatement of capacity/legal rep — the reinstated party or person appointed as legal representative; 4) in trustee duty termination — a new trustee; 5) in representative disqualification — a new representative or either party; 6) in bankruptcy trustee disqualification — an equally qualified person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific successor categories are authorized to resume depending on the interruption cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for resumption procedures and powers (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for resuming interrupted proceeding can be filed by persons in Article 21. The opposite party can request Commissioner/administrative patent judge to order the person to file the resumption request. Upon receipt, Commissioner/presiding judge shall notify opposite party. If, after ex officio examination, no grounds exist to accept the request, the Commissioner/judge shall dismiss it. Upon receipt of a request for resuming after service of certified decision/ruling, Commissioner/judge shall determine whether to permit resumption. If person fails to resume when ordered, Commissioner/judge shall ex officio order person to resume within specified period. If not resumed within that period, it shall be deemed resumed on day following expiration; Commissioner/judge shall notify relevant parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are detailed procedural steps for filing, notification, ex officio review, orders to resume, and deemed resumption if not acted on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proceeding — grounds and revocation (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Commissioner/administrative judge is unable to perform duties due to natural disaster or extenuating circumstances, proceedings shall be suspended until circumstances cease. If a relevant party is unable to resume due to an indefinite obstacle, Commissioner/judge may order suspension until obstacle removed. Commissioner/judge may revoke such determination. When suspension or revocation occurs, commissioner/judge shall notify all relevant parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension addresses office- or party-incapacity and includes notification and revocation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of interruption or suspension on running periods (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proceeding is interrupted or suspended, the running of the relevant period is interrupted, and the entire period restarts from the time the resumption of proceeding is notified or the proceeding is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interruptions/suspensions pause statutory deadlines and restart them upon resumption/notification.
